# Independent TMD2 qualified-reporting decision

**Accept the qualified reporting**, 2 November 2026, SCI-kfs-tmd2-reporting-agent-v1. This reviews the six questions in the historical `kfs-tmd2-appendix-law-v1/SCIENTIFIC_REVIEW.md`; that unsigned document remains unchanged. The outcome is specific to the source-informed TMD2 VW96+IGS operational reconstruction, definition SHA-256 `83777458ea437a3a7c1360117dbf435f7d763913cda399099ef2966e65a67e86`, its frozen constants/state, coordinates and saved evidence. It does not grant general IGS admission or close M1/M4, REV-04/REV-05, arbitrary-path, cyclic or finite-deformation gates.

Reviewer: separate Codex agent `/root/kfs_development_review`, explicitly dispatched by the coordinator under AGENTS.md. I did not author the target constitutive record, published-case selection, TMD2 requests/protocol, source-reference extraction, material observations, source-law packet or benchmark assessment. I previously reviewed distinct base-VW96 development reporting and database/web packaging interfaces. That prior work and access to the coordinator's conclusions are disclosed; I independently reread the primary pages and recomputed the saved arithmetic here. This is an actual separate-agent scoped scientific reporting decision, not a human signature or a claim to independent experimental authorship.

## Q1 — General host/IGS composition: accept with explicit domain qualifications

I visually inspected the exact [2016 paper](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11440-015-0402-z), PDF pp18–20, Appendix A Eqs7–19, and compared the archived/current target expressions. Eqs15–16 retain general beta and support beta=2.5; the beta=1 NH97 host specialization must not be substituted. Contracting Eq18 gives the stated two projection branches; under paired source/Atlas stress, strain and history sign changes the projection is unchanged and the nonlinear stress tensor changes sign. Eq19 requires no additional 1/R in history evolution. Source tensor contractions agree with Mandel weighting. VW96 PDFp2/printedp252 Eq2 supplies void-ratio continuity; NH97 PDFp2/printedp280 explicitly supplies negative compressive tensor conventions. These supplementary original pages were accessible and visually inspected.

The Jaumann rate reduces to the ordinary derivative only at the stated zero spin. Zero-history direction, near-isotropic regularization, capped rho, the 1% history admission band, runtime guards and finite-step subdivision are project choices, not printed Appendix A equations. Printed-law correspondence is supported on the physical history ball; stored accepted endpoints cannot prove internal-stage membership. The earlier exact 24 structural and ten Cartesian/Mandel tests independently replayed, but are algebraic coefficient-surrogate tests, not runtime material references. No Atlas evaluator was used.

## Q2 — Constants, stress scale and initial preparation: accept

2016 PDFp4 Table2 and 2019 PDFp3 Table1 visibly agree on all thirteen constants: phi=33.1 degrees; hs=4000 MPa; n=.27; ed0=.677; ec0=1.054; ei0=1.212; alpha=.14; beta=2.5; R=1e-4; mR=2.2; mT=1.1; beta_r=.1; chi=5.5. Their mR/mT column order differs; the named allocation is correct. hs becomes 4e9 Pa and phi is converted to radians. p_ref=100000 Pa is a separate project scale.

2016 Table3 PDFp5 identifies TMD2 as nominal p0=100 kPa, e0=.975, ID0=.21; Figure4a,b explicitly labels it. Section3.2 PDFp3 and 2019 PDFp3 prescribe mobilized isotropic history. Paired signs yield positive R/sqrt(3) diagonal history, zero shears and isotropic 100000 Pa stress. Saved parameter/state orders and all three requests match. Direct initialization is adequate for the declared published case; it does not recreate preceding physical consolidation. The measured first row and illustrative defaults remain separate.

The rounded stored history lies just inside the ball relative to the **actual binary64 request R** (rho squared minus one about -3.03e-17). Against ideal exact-decimal R it is about +6.55e-17. This rounding distinction is not an exact-real source-state or internal-stage inequality proof. My first checker used the wrong denominator for the stored-input claim; its failure and original script are retained.

## Q3 — Direct accumulated 0–25% coordinates: accept as operational reconstruction

I read the pinned driver mirror at lines392–399,632,664–668,892–903, without executing it: axial loading is mapped to uniform increments, accumulated strain is written directly, and comments identify logarithmic strain. The selected direct axial accumulation and normal-strain trace are therefore defensible declared operational coordinates. The 2019 Figure3a,b PDFp4 visually supports the selected lowest blue stress/highest blue volume curves and full displayed range. 2016 driver and 2019 Abaqus execution provenance remain distinct.

The exact historical decks, versions, finite-strain handling and plotting conversions are unavailable. Agreement with a plotted curve does not identify those choices. The error comparison also places a literal accumulated trace beside measured fractional volume change; it cannot establish finite-volume equivalence. These are blockers to historical-code/finite-deformation claims, **not** to this explicitly qualified reporting. The research CLI's .25 path must not be represented as extending the browser laboratory's .1 envelope.

## Q4 — Precision, criteria and retained failures: accept

The reference is a source-model curve extraction, not measurements. I regenerated it from the exact private SVG using the preserved extractor: SHA-256 `e2f0637c48cc068febc043079ed10f894789453de13fa8e97d149de4a0b3db92`, byte-identical. For independent chain-selection precision I rely on the earlier six-spot raster audit, whose method/receipts/results I inspected; I did not repeat that complete raster pipeline. The figure labels and axes were independently visually checked in the PDF. The two-full-stroke horizontal-window/vertical-expansion construction is a defensible conservative publication-precision policy, not a statistical confidence interval or parameter uncertainty estimate. Origin offsets are retained. Its q half-width is 6327.14 Pa and volume half-width .00177160; refinement limits are their tenths.

References, requests and constants match the preceding freeze exactly. The follow-up protocol changes its study ID and explicitly records the research range and superseded execution; common coordinate/comparison/error policies remain identical. Three original .1-cap rejections with zero points and the initial assessor's empty-prefix failure remain failures, not convergence results. The distinct .25 study retains 401/801/1601 points. My independent interpolation checks all six 101-coordinate source envelopes and four adjacent refinements. Maximum q changes are 16.9391 and 5.61394 Pa; volume changes 6.87084e-7 and 5.74396e-7. These do not prove global trajectory error or convergence order.

The frozen assessor's separate nonzero-process false-pass defect is real: an exit23 receipt could leave numerical gates true. I independently replayed the saved witness and revised supported guard: original valid frame accepted, exit23 rejected. Original receipts are integer zero with matching saved hashes, so that defect does not invalidate these particular saved paths. Historical assessor bytes and failure remain preserved; this review supplies no retrospective numerical gate.

## Q5 — Experimental errors: accept descriptive comparisons only

Using the exact private normalized file, I independently recomputed RMSE, MAE and maximum errors on the declared 101-coordinate measured overlap, retaining the last consecutive duplicate axial coordinate and rejecting reversals/extrapolation. All reported aggregates match. q RMSE is approximately 23.537–23.542 kPa; volume RMSE is .207738–.207740 percentage points. Their magnitude and the source's calibration descriptions (2016 PDFp3, 2019 PDFpp2–3/Table1) support the stated descriptive campaign role; agreement with the published numerical curve is not experimental predictive accuracy.

No held-out validation, model ranking, uncertainty estimate, physical finite-volume validation or measurement redistribution permission follows. The public reproduction figure was visually inspected and contains published model coordinates, Atlas predictions and the envelope, not measured curves. No measurement arrays, PDFs, SVGs or author implementation bytes are copied into this review. Aggregate values and source identity receipts do not confer redistribution rights.

## Q6 — Outcome and remaining gates

All five substantive questions support **accept qualified reporting**, with no unresolved blocker for that stated scope. Remaining qualifications are historical kinematic/output provenance; unobserved internal stages and source-versus-project integration/domain policy; broader host/IGS scientific and cyclic applicability; experimental independence/uncertainty; original-measurement reuse permission; and artifact/private-dependency durability. Portable summary bytes match the earlier study, but its reduced receipt packet shares frozen inputs and does not retain a second self-contained raw-output archive. Existing archived build/portable receipts are evidence of those recorded executions; I made no current build, material call or Wasm/experiment-browser validation.

The web snapshot's historical receipt says pending/unassigned. This decision may supersede that **reporting-pending claim only** through a separately scoped consumer update. It does not itself update the UI, approve model admission or establish deployment. The smallest next action is coordinator attachment of this exact verdict with the qualifications intact; broad scientific gates and rights remain independently tracked.

## Reproduce and evidence identity

`python3 -B docs/benchmarks/kfs-tmd2-reporting-agent-v1/check_saved.py` verifies public bindings, archived source identity, frozen inputs, original failures, saved source/refinement arithmetic and portable identity without private measurements or processes. Add `--private` to hash the seven available private inputs and recompute descriptive aggregates; it emits only aggregates and identities. `check-results.json` and `private-check-results.json` record the final executions. `replay-observations.json` records separately observed prior saved-only replay commands. These are integrity/arithmetic checks, not substitutes for the actual primary-source reading above.

`manifest.json` binds inspected/machine-consumed public files and review outputs; mutable readme/status statements are retained as exact snapshots under `inputs/statements/`, not bound to moving paths. Private access/coverage is recorded in `private-inputs.json`; all four primary PDFs were available and matched their recorded hashes. No claim is made that those private temporary inputs or local solver binaries are permanently retained. Two review-checker assumption failures are preserved under `retained-checker-attempt/`; neither changed original evidence or policy. The manifest and receipts do not assert a full transitive build/dependency closure. No build, fit, author-code execution, shared edit, admission, data release, commit, push or deployment was performed.
